The main US stock measures pointed lower in Wednesday's premarket activity as traders await minutes from the Federal Reserve's last policy meeting.

The S&P 500 edged down 0.1%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.3%, and the Nasdaq 100 was off 0.4%. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite finished Tuesday trading with record highs, while the Dow extended its rally for a fourth consecutive session.

The Fed is scheduled to post minutes of its September policy meeting at 2 pm ET, which will be assessed for fresh insight on the central bank's monetary policy trajectory. At that meeting, the central bank raised interest rates by 25 basis points, its first hike in just over three years, to combat inflation that has run persistently above its 2% target.

Markets are currently pricing in an 81% probability that the central bank will keep its benchmark rate steady later this month, with the remaining odds in favor of a 25-basis-point hike, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Treasury yields were trending upwards early Wednesday, with the two-year rate rising 1.7 basis points to 4.81% and the 10-year rate adding 5.5 basis points to 5.33%.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil inclined 0.7% to $90.03 a barrel, while Brent advanced 1.4% to $101.93.

About 20 commercial ships, mostly tankers, were attacked over the past month while sailing through the crucial Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf, or off the coast of Oman, CNBC reported Tuesday, citing the Joint Maritime Information Center.

Saudi Arabia's energy minister, Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman, said Tuesday that the Kingdom's East-West pipeline has increased crude flows to 5.8 million barrels per day, according to Reuters.

Shares of Constellation Brands (STZ) fell 5.2% pre-bell as the beer and wine company reiterated its full-year adjusted earnings outlook.

Penguin Solutions (PENG) jumped 6.1% after the company reported its latest financial results.

Denim maker Levi Strauss (LEVI) and Applied Digital (APLD) are scheduled to release their quarterly earnings after the markets close.

Spot gold retreated 1.1% to $4,142 per troy ounce, while bitcoin slumped 1.9% to $83,911.

US stock futures moved slightly lower on Wednesday as investors awaited minutes from the Federal Reserve's September policy meeting, while corporate developments at SpaceX, Constellation Brands and Levi Strauss were also in focus.

At 06:56 GMT, Dow futures were down 108 points, or 0.2%, while S&P 500 futures were broadly unchanged. Nasdaq 100 futures declined 28 points, or 0.1%.

The main Wall Street indices closed slightly higher in the previous session, although they finished below their intraday highs.

US and French government bond markets stabilised following recent selling, although benchmark 10-year yields moved higher. Analysts at Vital Knowledge said investors remained uncertain that "this asset class can sustain a material rally", citing increased artificial intelligence investment and an expected "tidal wave" of debt issuance.

Oil prices initially declined before recovering as investors assessed Middle Eastern crude shipments, transportation costs and the availability of refined products.

Investors Await Federal Reserve Minutes

The Federal Reserve is due to release minutes from its September meeting, when policymakers increased interest rates for the first time since 2023.

The Fed's projections indicated the possibility of further rate increases before the end of the year as policymakers continued to address inflation, which has remained above the central bank's 2% target.

However, market expectations for another increase at the Fed's next meeting have declined following comments from policymakers and weaker-than-expected employment data.

The minutes could provide additional information about policymakers' views on inflation, employment and the future path of interest rates.

SpaceX Reportedly Seeks $40 Billion for Nvidia Chip Purchases

SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) is seeking to raise approximately $40 billion to finance purchases of Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) chips, according to a Financial Times report citing people familiar with the matter.

The proposed financing would include approximately $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion of investment-grade debt, according to the report.

Apollo Global (NYSE:APO) is expected to lead the financing and assist with marketing the debt, while Pimco is reportedly among a group of potential lenders.

The financing would support purchases of computing infrastructure used for artificial intelligence. Elon Musk has previously said SpaceX would exclusively use Nvidia chips in its Colossus data centres.

^NDX
QQQ

Trading disclosure

A narrow group of artificial intelligence companies is driving the Nasdaq 100 Index to all-time highs, creating classic "low breadth" conditions often seen ahead of a market bubble, BofA said.

Analysts recommend using call option spreads on tech ETFs like Invesco QQQ to secure upside potential while capping downside equity exposure.

According to Bank of America's proprietary Bubble Risk Indicator, U.S. technology equities currently show the highest warning metrics among global asset classes.

Market strategists at Bank of America Corp. (BAC) are alerting investors to potential bubble dynamics forming in the technology sector, while advising a controlled, derivative-based approach to remain invested.

The Nasdaq 100 Index has reached fresh highs despite pressure from rising Treasury yields. However, market observers highlight that the advance is largely concentrated in a handful of mega-cap artificial intelligence firms rather than broad market participation.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Longer-duration yields have hit multi-decade highs, but tech stocks have been resilient so far to the risks of soaring yields.

"Low breadth is a classic feature of bubbles building and typically doesn't stop until they pop," Bank of America strategists Arjun Goyal, Riddhi Prasad, and Benjamin Bowler wrote in a note to clients.

Mitigating Downside via Equity Derivatives

To address concerns among fund managers who fear underperforming benchmark indexes, the bank's strategy team advises using derivative contracts over direct equity positions.

Specifically, the strategists recommend buying call options and call spreads on the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ), an exchange-traded fund that tracks the Nasdaq 100. This structure lets market participants capture further gains while limiting potential losses if tech shares pull back suddenly. To offset option premiums, institutional investors can sell downside protection on the index.

For advanced institutional trading desks, the team also suggested exotic options structured to pay out if the technology index continues to climb in a rising-rate environment.

Bubble Indicators Point to Elevated Risk Levels

The advisory comes as internal analytics show growing valuation risks in major equity indexes. Bank of America tracks market frothiness across 32 asset classes, equity sectors, commodities, and cryptocurrencies through its proprietary Bubble Risk Indicator (BRI).
